benchmarks.note: continuous fit with automatic xmin. alpha is closed-form per candidate xmin, but the xmin scan visits the distinct data values; for continuous Pareto draws nearly every value is unique, so the scan is ~O(num_uniques) closed-form evaluations each O(n) over the kept tail → roughly quadratic in n (the 5000 point is ~20x the 1000 point). This mirrors upstream igraph_plfit_continuous's xmin loop

discrete fit with automatic xmin. Each candidate xmin runs a golden-section maximisation whose objective evaluates a Hurwitz-zeta (Euler-Maclaurin) term — heavier per candidate than the continuous closed form — but the integer-valued data collapses to a small number of distinct candidate xmins, so the total candidate count barely grows with n and runtime scales sub-linearly. At n=200 the fixed golden-section + zeta cost dominates, making small-n discrete slower than small-n continuous
